key_insight: Coding agents can directly search for compact, explicit flow-control rules that rival or beat deep reinforcement learning while staying interpretable.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical path to active flow control controllers that are easier to inspect, debug, and transfer across fluid regimes than black-box neural policies.
method: Use a constrained heuristic-learning loop where an agent proposes executable feedback laws.
Evaluate and revise controllers only through the public benchmark simulator interface.
Compare discovered controllers against strong DRL baselines under the same simulation budget across 13 flow-control benchmarks.
evidence_signal: Across 13 benchmarks in 1D, 2D, and 3D active flow-control problems, the heuristic controllers matched or outperformed the best DRL policy in 10 cases under identical simulation budgets.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of the benchmark interface and search protocol, so generalization to unseen geometries or poorly specified action/observation spaces still needs careful validation.
paper_title: Heuristic Learning for Active Flow Control Using Coding Agents
